units.t: Review: Present Tense and Irregular Verbs

learn: -ar: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. -er: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en. -ir: -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en.
The present expresses habits, current actions and near-future plans.
"Estudio español todos los días" means "I study Spanish every day."
lessons.try: Write a paragraph about your typical week.

learn: Some verbs are irregular only in the yo form: hago (hacer), pongo (poner), salgo (salir), traigo (traer), conozco (conocer), sé (saber).
Others are fully irregular: ser, estar, ir, tener, venir, decir.
Saber is knowing facts; conocer is knowing people and places.
check: The yo form of salir is...
"Conozco a María" uses conocer because María is...
The yo form of saber is...
lessons.try: Write sentences using five irregular yo forms.

learn: e → ie (pensar), o → ue (poder), e → i (pedir), u → ue (jugar).
Changes happen in all forms except nosotros and vosotros (the "boot").
"¿Puedes ayudarme?" means "Can you help me?"
lessons.try: Draw the "boot" for three stem-changing verbs.

learn: Reflexive verbs show that the subject acts on itself: lavarse (to wash oneself).
Reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nos, os, se.
"Me levanto a las siete" means "I get up at seven."
lessons.try: Conjugate levantarse and ducharse.

learn: Despertarse (wake up), levantarse (get up), ducharse, cepillarse los dientes, vestirse, peinarse, acostarse.
Sequence words: primero, luego, después, más tarde, finalmente.
Many are also stem-changing: me despierto, me visto, me acuesto.
lessons.try: Describe your morning routine in order.

learn: With an infinitive, attach the pronoun to the end or put it before the conjugated verb: "Voy a ducharme" or "Me voy a duchar."
Both mean "I'm going to shower."
Reflexive verbs can also show reciprocal actions: "Nos vemos" (We see each other).
check: Another way to say "Voy a ducharme" is...
lessons.try: Write five plans using reflexive infinitives.

learn: The preterite describes completed actions in the past.
-ar endings: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron.
"Hablé con mi abuela ayer" means "I spoke with my grandmother yesterday."
lessons.try: Write five things you did last weekend.

learn: -er/-ir endings: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron.
"Comí paella" (I ate paella). "Escribieron una carta" (They wrote a letter).
Nosotros forms of -ar and -ir verbs are the same in present and preterite; context tells you which.
lessons.try: Write a short account of a meal you ate.

learn: Verbs ending in -car, -gar, -zar change in the yo form: busqué, llegué, empecé.
Leer and oír: leyó, leyeron; oyó, oyeron.
Time expressions: ayer, anoche (last night), la semana pasada, el año pasado, hace dos días.
check: The yo preterite of llegar is...
lessons.try: Write a diary entry about yesterday.

units.t: The Preterite: Irregular and Stem-Changing Verbs

learn: Ser and ir share the same preterite forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron.
Context shows the meaning: "Fui al cine" (I went); "Fue un día bonito" (It was a nice day).
These are among the most common past forms.
lessons.try: Write three sentences each with fue meaning "went" and "was".

learn: Many verbs have irregular stems with endings -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron (no accents).
Tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud-, poner → pus-, hacer → hic- (hizo), venir → vin-, querer → quis-.
Decir → dij- and traer → traj- use -eron: dijeron.
check: The preterite yo of tener is...
lessons.try: Make flashcards for ten irregular preterite stems.

learn: -ir stem-changers change in the third person: pedir → pidió, pidieron; dormir → durmió, durmieron.
-ar and -er stem-changers do not change in the preterite.
"Mi hermano durmió diez horas."
lessons.try: Conjugate preferir and servir in the preterite.

learn: -ar: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. -er/-ir: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían.
Only three irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía).
"Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque."
lessons.try: Conjugate jugar, comer and vivir in the imperfect.

learn: The imperfect describes habitual past actions ("I used to..."), ongoing actions, descriptions, time and age in the past.
"Eran las ocho" (It was eight o'clock). "Tenía diez años" (I was ten).
Signal words: siempre, a menudo (often), todos los días, mientras (while).
lessons.try: Describe your house when you were little.

learn: Toys and games: los juguetes, la muñeca (doll), el columpio (swing), jugar al escondite (hide-and-seek).
"De niño/niña..." means "As a child..."
Describe people, places and routines from childhood.
lessons.try: Write a paragraph beginning "De niño/niña..."

learn: Preterite: completed actions, specific times, sequences of events.
Imperfect: background, descriptions, habits, ongoing actions.
Think of the imperfect as the stage set and the preterite as the action.
check: "Ayer comí pizza" uses the preterite for...
lessons.try: Sort twenty sentences into preterite and imperfect.

learn: An ongoing action (imperfect) is interrupted by another (preterite): "Leía cuando sonó el teléfono."
"Mientras" usually introduces the imperfect.
"De repente" (suddenly) usually introduces the preterite.
check: "Leía cuando sonó el teléfono": the interruption is...
lessons.try: Write five interrupted-action sentences.

learn: Use the imperfect to set the scene and the preterite to move the plot.
Verbs with different meanings: conocí (I met) versus conocía (I knew); supe (I found out) versus sabía (I knew).
Combine both tenses to tell a vivid story.
check: In stories, the preterite moves the...
lessons.try: Retell a fairy tale in the past using both tenses.

learn: Direct object pronouns replace the thing or person receiving the action: me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las.
"Compro el libro" becomes "Lo compro."
They go before a conjugated verb or attach to an infinitive.
check: "Voy a comprarlo" attaches lo to the...
lessons.try: Rewrite ten sentences using direct object pronouns.

learn: Indirect object pronouns show to whom or for whom: me, te, le, nos, os, les.
"Le doy el regalo a mi madre" means "I give the gift to my mother."
Le and les are often clarified with "a + person".
lessons.try: Write sentences about giving gifts to family members.

learn: When both appear, indirect comes before direct: "Me lo das."
Le and les become se before lo, la, los, las: "Se lo doy."
"¿Me lo explicas?" means "Will you explain it to me?"
lessons.try: Answer five questions using double object pronouns.

learn: El menú, la cuenta, la propina (tip), el plato principal, el postre (dessert).
Ordering: "Para mí, el pollo, por favor." "¿Qué me recomienda?"
Describing food: rico, picante (spicy), salado (salty), dulce.
lessons.try: Role-play ordering a three-course meal.

learn: Affirmative tú commands use the él form: ¡Come! ¡Escribe!
Irregulars: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven.
Negative tú commands use the subjunctive form: ¡No comas! ¡No hables!
check: The affirmative tú command of hacer is...
lessons.try: Write five instructions for making a sandwich.

learn: Usted commands use the subjunctive: ¡Coma! ¡Escriba! ¡Hable!
Recipes often use formal or infinitive commands: "Corte las cebollas."
Pronouns attach to affirmative commands: "Cómalo."
check: The usted command of hablar is...
lessons.try: Write a family recipe in Spanish using usted commands.

units.t: Health, the Body and the Present Progressive

learn: La cabeza, el brazo, la mano, la pierna, el pie, el estómago, la garganta (throat), los ojos.
"Me duele la cabeza" means "My head hurts" (doler works like gustar).
"Me duelen los pies" uses duelen with plural.
lessons.try: Play "Simón dice" with body parts.

learn: "Estoy enfermo/a." "Tengo fiebre" (fever), "tengo tos" (cough), "tengo un resfriado" (a cold).
The doctor: "Tome estas pastillas." "Descanse."
"La receta" is the prescription.
check: "La receta" at the doctor's is the...
lessons.try: Role-play a visit to the doctor.

learn: Estar + present participle (-ando/-iendo) shows actions happening right now.
"Estoy estudiando" (I am studying). "Están comiendo" (They are eating).
Irregulars: leyendo, durmiendo, pidiendo, diciendo.
check: The present participle of dormir is...
The present progressive uses estar plus...
lessons.try: Describe what five family members are doing right now.

learn: Más... que (more than), menos... que (less than), tan... como (as... as).
Irregulars: mejor (better), peor (worse), mayor (older), menor (younger).
Superlatives: el/la más... de: "Es la ciudad más grande de México."
lessons.try: Compare three cities using comparisons and superlatives.

learn: El aeropuerto, el pasaporte, la maleta (suitcase), el billete/boleto (ticket), el hotel, la reserva.
"Quisiera reservar una habitación."
"¿A qué hora sale el tren?"
check: "¿A qué hora sale el tren?" asks...
lessons.try: Plan a trip to a Spanish-speaking city.

learn: Spanish-speaking countries span Europe, the Americas and Africa (Equatorial Guinea).
Each has unique foods, music, dialects and traditions.
Respectful curiosity helps you connect with people from other cultures.
check: Spanish is official in Equatorial Guinea, in...
lessons.try: Research one country and present its culture in Spanish.
